scope: Version direct constant-bitmask indexes with one invariant upper-bound guard, allowing this bounded case to duplicate a single-check scalar loop.
patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/loops.jo b/core/compiler/loops.jo
index 5b252618..2d0fe8ed 100644
--- a/core/compiler/loops.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/loops.jo
@@ -90,7 +90,7 @@ struct LCheck:
     pend: int           # its end
     pc: int             # the comparison it tests (gone with it in the copy, when used only there)
     kind: int           # 0: index x + k against len (x the counter), 1: invariant index x, 2: null arr
-    x: int              # kind 3 records the original shifted-index vreg
+    x: int              # kind 3: shifted-index vreg; kind 5: constant unsigned index bound
     k: int
     len: int
     terms: int[]        # kind 3: counter + terms + k; kind 4: invariant terms + k
@@ -182,6 +182,21 @@ lx_checks = (code: Ins[], ends: int[], L: CLoop) -> LCheck[]:
                 out.push(LCheck(p, q, d, 1, x, 0, len, []))
                 continue
             xd = lx_def_at(code, x, L.pl + 1, L.inc)
+            # Every bitwise-and result is <= either operand as an unsigned word.
+            # Require the one definition to precede this check on the same
+            # structured path: crossing an end/else could leave an older value
+            # when that definition's conditional branch was not taken.
+            if xd >= 0 and xd < d and d < p and code[xd].op == .and_:
+                bound = -1
+                if is_kv(int(code[xd].b)): bound = int(code[xd].b)
+                else if is_kv(int(code[xd].a)): bound = int(code[xd].a)
+                if bound >= 0:
+                    dominates = true
+                    loop j in [xd + 1..p):
+                        if code[j].op == .end or code[j].op == .else_: dominates = false
+                    if dominates:
+                        out.push(LCheck(p, q, d, 5, bound, 0, len, []))
+                        continue
             if xd >= 0 and code[xd].op == .add and int(code[xd].a) == L.ctr and is_kv(int(code[xd].b)) and lx_def_at(code, L.ctr, L.pl + 1, L.inc) < 0:
                 out.push(LCheck(p, q, d, 0, L.ctr, kv_of(int(code[xd].b)), len, []))
                 continue
@@ -709,8 +724,10 @@ loop_versioning = (vector_only: bool = false):
         plan = VPlan(false, 0, false, [], [], [], [])
         if lx_vec_on: plan = lx_vec_plan(code, L, checks, first, last)
         if vector_only and not plan.ok: continue
-        # (one check costs about as much as testing for it in front: not worth a copy)
-        if not plan.ok and checks.len() < 2: continue
+        # Usually require several checks to repay loop duplication. A fixed mask
+        # bound can also eliminate one recurring ring-buffer/table check.
+        if not plan.ok and checks.len() < 2:
+            if checks.len() == 0 or checks[0].kind != 5: continue
         loop p in [at..L.pl): out.push(code[p])
         wrap = 0
         if checks.len() > 0:
@@ -763,7 +780,7 @@ loop_versioning = (vector_only: bool = false):
                 hi = lx_bin(out, .add, upper, ov)
                 lx_fail(out, lx_bin(out, .gtu, lo, hi))
                 lx_fail(out, lx_bin(out, .geu, hi, ch.len))
-            else if ch.kind == 1: lx_fail(out, lx_bin(out, .geu, ch.x, ch.len))
+            else if ch.kind == 1 or ch.kind == 5: lx_fail(out, lx_bin(out, .geu, ch.x, ch.len))
             else if ch.kind == 4: lx_fail(out, lx_bin(out, .geu, lx_sum(code, L, ch.terms, ch.k, out), ch.len))
             else: lx_fail(out, lx_bin(out, .eq, ch.x, k_vreg(0)))
         # the copy without the checks: values made and used only in the loop get names of their own

limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.

limits: A 2% timing resolution is not a per-stage slowdown budget; compare both references.
Bootstrap intervals are approximate; inconclusive results require an isolated recheck.
Passing measured budgets does not establish language completeness or universal C parity.

decision: The focused pilot suggested about 3% release improvement, but the independent C-bootstrap full stage did not reproduce a useful gain on either permanent managed-parameter workload. Four of 52 comparisons were inconclusive. Do not collect additional rechecks to accept complexity without demonstrated benefit. Retain behavioral edge cases; remove the assertion requiring the experimental versioned loop.
notes: The pilot uses C -O3 -march=native; permanent stage uses C -O2.
The accepted compiler and performance baseline remain checker-exposure/94952e82. This report is not an accepted stage certificate.
